dedupe_keys.name: joplin tornado 2011 evacuation of st john s regional medical center and the storm hardened rebuild

description: This case study describes what happened to hospital care in Joplin, Missouri, when an EF-5 tornado struck on 22 May 2011, and how the destroyed hospital was rebuilt to resist wind. It is published by the U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a federal website, drawing on Mercy Hospital Joplin and Freeman Health System, and is free to read online. The tornado killed 161 people and injured about 1,371, and hit St. John's Regional Medical Center directly, blowing out windows and destroying generators; staff evacuated 183 patients and visitors in 90 minutes using wheelchairs, backboards and doors, but five critical-care patients and one visitor died. The nearby Freeman hospital, running on generators, received critical patients, 70 to 100 ambulances within four hours and about 400 patients in triage, and prepared for a water outage; a 60-bed field hospital opened within a week. The replacement hospital, opened in March 2015, has a precast concrete shell, wind-resistant windows and partially buried generators. Coverage is one city. Caveats: the account is a short narrative from the hospitals, not an independent review. Simulation uses: an observed case for hospital evacuation, surge and backup power failure in healthcare resilience models. Related records: the IN-CORE Joplin testbed (case_study-joplin-in-core-testbed) models the same tornado's community impacts.
